claims.text: In the same episode Borland argued that because AARO holds no original classification authority it had to refer his account out to the intelligence community and to private companies for a classification determination, and that his triangle account coming back unclassified while other drawings were classified is therefore itself evidence about what was seen: 'they would have to be classified' (2:23:27). Nothing opened for this board establishes AARO's classification authority either way; this is recorded as his argument.

label: Dylan Borland
narrative: Dylan Borland is a US Air Force veteran who testified publicly for the first time on 9 September 2025 before the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, describing a 2012 UAP encounter at Langley Air Force Base and, more consequentially for the record, what happened to him afterwards. His testimony to the task force: 'My professional career was deliberately obstructed, and I have endured sustained reprisals.' He described witnesses in his position as feeling 'discarded, isolated, hopeless' after coming forward. Borland's value on this board is as a reprisal datum rather than a phenomenology datum: the hearing was titled 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection,' and the minority witness was POGO's Joe Spielberger on whistleblower channels, which means the majority and minority converged on the proposition that the existing protections do not work for this class of witness. Langley is also not an incidental location - it is the base whose December 2023 drone incursions became a congressional issue in their own right, and a 2012 UAP encounter there sits inside the same air-defence problem set.
